stories.title: Pakistan’s mineral exploration increasingly focused on strategic resources, minister tells investors
summary: Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said on Friday that Pakistan’s exploration efforts were increasingly focused on minerals that were of strategic importance to global investors.
He was addressing the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 (PMIF26) in Islamabad, where delegations, exhibitors and attendees have arrived from across the world to attend the event.

As the two-day event opened on Thursday, Pakistan showcased its vast mineral resources, ranging from coal and salt to gold and critical minerals, to attract international investment, promising predictable, investor-friendly policies, institutional support and security.

stories.title: Delhi overtakes Lahore as world's most polluted major city as air quality deteriorates
summary: India’s capital, Delhi, overtook Lahore to become the world’s most polluted city on Friday, with air quality reaching hazardous levels and visibility dropping as smog blanketed the city of 20 million people.

Earlier, Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) stood at 334, categorised as “hazardous”, making it the most polluted major city globally, according to Swiss air quality monitoring group IQAir, which measures pollution levels based on the concentration of pollutants.
Earlier this week, Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration was eight times the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) guideline value, according to a report by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI).

stories.title: Democratic US Senator Chris Van Hollen announces run for US Senate majority leader, challenging Schumer
summary: Democratic US Senator Chris Van Hollen said on Thursday he would run for Senate majority leader, challenging Chuck Schumer, who has led the Democrats in the Senate since 2017, after the Democratic Party won a majority in the chamber in the midterm elections.

Schumer, who is expected to retain his party’s leadership in the chamber but previously predicted not having a challenger, released his own statement on Thursday saying he had the votes to continue as the Democratic leader in the Senate.

Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont, an independent who caucuses with Democrats, said they would support Van Hollen, who has been a US senator for nearly a decade and spent 14 years before that in the House of Representatives.

stories.title: Lahore High Court moved against change of names of universities
summary: LAHORE: A petition has been filed in the Lahore High Court, challenging the removal of the word “university” from the names of six public sector varsities and demanding restoration of their former title of “college”.

The petition contends that the amendment arbitrarily downgraded the nomenclature of the institutions without consulting the stakeholders, including vice chancellors, faculty members, academic bodies and students.

stories.title: OECD report reveals migration to developed countries is dwindling
summary: PARIS: Migration to developed countries dwindled for a second year in a row in 2025, down 1.6pc compared to the previous year, according to an OECD report published on Thursday.
The United States saw a 14pc drop, although it still leads OECD countries, recording more than 1.2m permanent migrants in 2025.
The 1.1m asylum applications in 2025 marked a 22pc decrease to OECD countries, excluding the United States, compared with the previous year, although remaining about 10pc higher than 2019 figures.
